newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MTBE down, Saudi MTBE glitch may pressure Sep.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MTBE down, Saudi MTBE glitch may pressure Sep.

text.p: Spot MTBE prices eased in slow trade on Thursday amid a continuing suspension of demand, but some traders said they fear September values may strengthen on unconfirmed talk Saudi Arabia's 16,000 bpd plant has been idled by a mechanical problem.
The plant, a joint venture between Saudi Arabia Basic Industries Corp and Shell Oil, has apparently been down since Sunday due to a mechanical problem in the unit that makes isobutylene.
Downtime has been estimated at anywhere from two weeks to two months, according to traders.
Neither SABIC nor Shell could be reached for comment.

"The news probably wouldn't affect the prompt month but we could see some strength in the back end of August or September because that is when we were expecting to see material from SABIC arrive in the U.S.," said a Houston player.
About 70 percent of the material from the recently launched plant was expected to be marketed in the U.S., according to industry players.
Meanwhile, in the fifth consecutive slow day of trade for the prompt cycle, MTBE in the U.S. Gulf dipped about 1.25 cent since Tuesday to put offers at 95.00 cents a gallon.
New York Harbor was a little more active, with a small parcel heard sold at 100.00 cents a gallon.
"No one absolutely has to buy barrels today or tomorrow to blend with gasoline and with the market backwardated buyers are waiting, hoping to get lower numbers" said a Gulf producer.
